source: Burns, Fu & Constantino, PLOS ONE 2019;14(3):e0214029 (7 methods vs DXA, n=437); plus DoD tape vs HW/BIA/skinfolds conference abstract (Int J Exerc Sci Conf Proc 14(1) #40)
attribution: Burns et al., PLOS ONE 2019
coverage: Mean differences vs DXA: HW 1.0, skinfolds 1.4, ADP 1.6, Valhalla 4-electrode BIA 1.6, Omron hand-held 4.9; equivalence +-10% (= +-2.7 points): skinfolds, ADP, 4-electrode BIA, HW; not equivalent: Tanita foot-to-foot, Omron, near-infrared (Tanita equivalent at +-15%); MAPE 11.7% (skinfolds) to 21.9% (Omron)
sample_note: Read from the article text (Results/Discussion); Tanita and NIR mean differences are only in the Table 3 image, so not quoted
notes: Sample: college students, mean age 19.2, fit; errors grow at higher body fat. DoD abstract: n=69, LoA wider than +-3.5 points. CMB-020 (PMC6426203 re-read 2026-10-28): the skinfold method is a seven-site assessment (chest, midaxillary, triceps, subscapular, abdomen, suprailiac, thigh; Lange caliper, right side, two rotating measurements and a third if they differ by more than 2 mm; Siri; the equation is not named, the paper cites Jackson and Pollock 1978 and Jackson, Pollock and Ward 1980); N = 437 (301 women, 136 men), mean age 19.2; skinfolds mean difference from DXA 1.4% (90% CI 1.1-1.7, Table 3); title "Measurement agreement in percent body fat estimates among laboratory and field assessments in college students: Use of equivalence testing". Table 3 column "Mean Difference (DXA–Surrogate; % Body Fat)": skinfolds +1.4, so they read 1.4 points below DXA on average (a signed mean, not a typical miss: the page says "read 1.4 points below" and gives the MAPE, 11.7%, as the average miss); MAPE lowest of the seven methods, hydrostatic weighing the smallest mean difference (1.0); "Trained graduate students performed the skinfolds thickness measurements". CMB-021 (PMC6426203 re-read 2026-10-29): Table 3 "Agreement in percent body fat estimates compared to dual-emission X-ray absorptiometry", all seven rows (DXA minus method in points, 90% CI, MAPE): hydrostatic weighing 1.0 (0.6-1.4) 13.4%; skinfold thickness 1.4 (1.1-1.7) 11.7%; ADP 1.6 (1.3-1.9) 14.5%; IR 4.2 (3.7-4.7) 18.7%; Omron BIA 4.9 (4.5-5.3) 21.9%; Tanita BIA 3.5 (3.0-4.0) 17.2%; Valhalla BIA 1.6 (1.1-2.1) 17.0%. 10% equivalence interval -2.7 to 2.7 ("+/- 10% of the criterion mean, which corresponded to +/- 2.7% body fat"): hydrostatic weighing, skinfolds, ADP and Valhalla BIA equivalent; at 15% "all surrogate assessments, except for Omron BIA and IR". Table 1: DXA 27.0% (SD 7.6) overall (its women and men rows, 28.2 and 20.8, do not average to it with 301 and 136: not used). Table 4: "differences between DXA and each surrogate assessment increased as mean percent body fat increased", all but Valhalla BIA (r = 0.04, p = 0.784). Devices: DXA Hologic Discovery W (software 12.1); BOD POD (COSMED), seated, two volume measurements; Futrex-6100 A/ZL light wand on the belly of the biceps; OMRON HBF-306 handheld, arms extended; Tanita BF-556 two-electrode foot-to-foot scale; Valhalla Scientific Model 1990B, four electrodes on the right hand and foot, supine; hydrostatic weighing on an underwater swing after full exhalation. Pre-test: large meals avoided 2 hours, vigorous exercise 12 hours, alcohol 48 hours, liquids limited to 2 glasses of water at least 2 hours before, bladder emptied immediately before; "dehydration can lead to overestimation of percent body fat", "overhydration can lead to underestimation". Machine-readable copy: research/how-to-measure-body-fat-build/burns_2019_table3.json. The endpoint (a WKU conference abstract on the military tape method) is no longer cited by /blog/how-to-measure-body-fat/: Foulis 2023 (foulis-2023-circumference-dxa) replaces it.
